verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 4.0 'Long numbers' (under the heading '4.0 Rules common to every tool [D]'): 'A value of more than 12 digits is shown shortened ("1.2345... x 10^83", with the number of digits), with the exact digits in the table view, in the tooltip and in every export.' SPEC 4 T5 (phase 3): 'Tape: the list of numbers fired so far.' and 'Two games compared: ... overlay the two tapes sorted'. The sentence supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: Read at f07eec6 (worktree detached there, git status empty). The 4.0 sentence has no qualifier: no 'may', no exception for lists or tapes. 4.0 carries [D] on its heading, but a tape printed in full departs from the [D] text rather than choosing within it. T5 is phase 3 (SPEC 4 table: 'T5 Numbers Game Lab | numbers | 3'; heading 'T5. Numbers Game Lab (phase 3)') and the gate is G6. A reader can reach it. SPEC 6.6 Validation refuses only 'a start with an entry longer than 40 digits', and decisions/P3-A3.md 'the start chooser' lets the custom field take 'at most 40 digits', so a 20-digit start is both valid and typeable. Source at the gate: T05NumbersGameLab.svelte:214-215 'listText = (v) => v.map(display).join', and tuple feeds data-out="tape" (:601), endA and endB (:795, :798). The cells snippet (:552-553) feeds sortedA and sortedB (:787-788). display only swaps the minus sign. Records checked: decisions/P3-A3.md and DECISIONS.md:1671 'P3-A3: long numbers' cover the products D and M only; 'Plain lists of integers stay text' (P3-A3, formulas entry) concerns MathML against text, not shortening. RT-FIX-P3-export-long (DECISIONS.md:2574) fixed only the dimension (P3-RT-03-03), and RT-FIX-P5-t12-content (DECISIONS.md:3382) only T12's string viewer. No decision exempts the tape, the sorted tapes or the end positions. reports/gate-G6.md (its line 3 names gate commit f07eec6) records no open item on T5 long numbers. No merge-P6-redteam report exists on disk. The known-and-decided list of P6-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS has nothing on it. No oracle value is involved, since this is display only. incidental: the 'Start: custom, (...)' line (data-out="startKind", :572) uses the same tuple helper.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 4.0 has no permitting clause for tapes or lists; R2 the finding quotes 4.0 exactly; R3 T5 is phase 3 at gate G6; R4 no oracle value is in question; R5 4.0 is [D] but printing in full departs from its text, and P3-A3 and RT-FIX-P3-export-long cover only the products and the dimension; R6 no record in gate-G6.md or in an earlier round's open items. A stated behaviour that is wrong is major, as P3-RT-03-03 and P5-RT-03-01 were.

verdicts.citation: CONTRACTS.md 4 (worker.ts): 'Serialization: ... Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard); errors re-thrown on the main side as the same class.' CONTRACTS 4 state.ts: resolveBoard 'throws on not-a-board'. SPEC 5.1 E-9 item 3: 'Satake data (satake, satakeRecord, restrictedBoard) for E7 and E8' run 'in a Web Worker behind a promise'. The relabelling half follows the contract's own serialization. The never-settling promise has no text that permits it.
verdicts.evidence: Part (b), the named restricted board coming back as the standard board: CONTRACTS 4 prescribes exactly this round trip, and BoardSpec = string | { cartan; xy? } has no labels. It is also a logged and known consequence. DECISIONS.md:455 (P1-A2): 'a board { "$board": BoardSpec } (its name, or { cartan } from cartanNumbers) ... a sub-board's labels ... are not carried; noted'. DECISIONS.md:2247 (MERGE, phase 4): 'workerWire.ts serialises any named board by its name, so a board whose positions are not in its name's standard order (a folded board, later a restricted board of phase 6) would be rebuilt in the worker with its positions permuted ... a lead for RT-06 and P6-A1'. DECISIONS.md:3520 (MERGE on P6-A1) notes e8(-24) among the 7 named restricted boards whose matrix stays in orbit order. The finding's 'behind the same promise ... same result' is not E-9's wording, which reads 'behind a promise'; it comes from worker.ts's header comment. Part (a), the 0-node board: MERGE ruling (4) on P6-A1 (DECISIONS.md:3520) makes the restricted board of a compact form 'n 0'. resolveBoard refuses it. worker.ts:137 'if (reply.ok) p.resolve(deserialize(reply.result))' has no catch, and the entry is already deleted from pending at :136, so the throw escapes onmessage and the promise never settles. P1-A2's record says only 'A worker error event rejects every pending call', and worker.ts:5 says 'a worker failure rejects the promise'. No sentence permits a pending promise. Reachability: decisions/P6-A3.md:37 'A pair with no white node gets the empty restricted board without a call' (t13/load.ts noWhiteNode), so no reader reaches (a) through T13. This bears on severity only. Not in gate-G6.md open items. Not in the known-and-decided list.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 holds only for the relabelling half (CONTRACTS 4 prescribes 'Board as its BoardSpec (rebuilt with resolveBoard)', logged by P1-A2 and passed on by MERGE in phase 4), but no text permits an engineCall promise that never settles after a valid worker result; R2 the finding misquotes E-9 ('same promise', 'same result'), but its cause stands on CONTRACTS 4 and engineCall's promise; R3 restrictedBoard and E-9 item 3 are phase 6 at G6; R4 no oracle value is in question; R5 no recorded decision accepts the hang; R6 the phase 4 MERGE lead covers only the relabelling and is not a tracked red-team finding. Minor fits, since no reader reaches either effect (P6-A3: no call without a white node).

verdicts.citation: decisions/P6-A5.md '2026-10-25 P6-A5: the TikZ forms': 'a coordinate that is not a finite number below 1e15 in size throws RangeError, as does an edge that does not join two given vertices or a label list of the wrong length.' CONTRACTS.md 4: 'exportLaTeX(kind, data: unknown): string; // phase 6 (P6-A5)'. SPEC.md 6.7 is silent on refusals. The recorded decision supports the finding's expected.
verdicts.evidence: SPEC 6.7 (read whole) says only that orbit graphs and projections 'are exported as plain TikZ coordinates'. It has no sentence that permits or forbids malformed data. CONTRACTS 4 gives only the signature, phase 6. The refusal rule is P6-A5's recorded decision, quoted above, together with export.ts:736 'Throws RangeError, naming the fault, on data it cannot write'. An edge [<hole>, 1], or an edge to a vertex that is a hole, does not 'join two given vertices', so by P6-A5's own record it must throw. Source at f07eec6: edgeList (:689) checks pairs with e.every, which skips holes; tikzGraph (:700) uses nodes.map and tikzPoints (:713, :723) uses points.map and forEach, all of which skip holes. No decision in DECISIONS.md, decisions/P6-A5.md or decisions/P6-tikz.md mentions holes or sparse lists. The same class of defect, 'a population with a hole that passes the input check', was ruled a minor and fixed in P6-A1's repair (DECISIONS.md:3520, 3708). exportLaTeX is phase 6 (CONTRACTS 4; SPEC 4.0 'LaTeX export ... arrives in phase 6'). Not in gate-G6.md. Not in the known-and-decided list (which holds only TikZ edge colours and labels). Reachability: T2's and T10's adapters build dense arrays (the finding says so), so only code reaches it.
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 neither SPEC 6.7 nor CONTRACTS 4 permits writing 'undefined' or undefined node names, and P6-A5's record says such an edge throws; R2 the finding reads the docstring and the P6-A5 decision correctly; R3 exportLaTeX is phase 6 at G6; R4 no oracle value is involved; R5 no [D] or recorded decision accepts holes; R6 no record. Minor fits for an input check that only code can reach.

verdicts.citation: R2: CONTRACTS.md 2.3 'Caps (src/caps.ts, plan)' is only the CAPS constants block ('countGamesGroup: 60000, ...'), and 2.1 row 'src/caps.ts | the numbers of section 5.6 as named constants'. Neither holds the finding's 'caps come from CAPS and are used once'. SPEC.md 5.6 row 'Group order for counting games | 60000 | count not offered' is the number the page states. The wording is the plan's and is recorded: build-plan/agents/P6-A4-t14-atlas.md item 13 'show a sentence that the count is not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements (wording plan)'; decisions/P6-A4.md '2026-10-25 P6-A4: the items as shown' and 'the downloads (plan formats)', both copied into DECISIONS.md.
verdicts.evidence: The finding's expected cites 'CONTRACTS 2.3: caps come from CAPS and are used once.' At f07eec6, CONTRACTS 2.3 is a heading and a code block and says nothing about use. 'Used once' appears only in the title of RT-03 lens attack 36, a red-team plan line. RED-TEAM-COMMON 2 defines a finding as a disagreement with 'the specification, the oracle, or the contract'. The behaviour the contract and SPEC govern is correct. atlasData.ts:280 'const completeGames = W <= CAPS.countGamesGroup ? countCompleteGames(board) : null', which is the comparison P6-A4 item 13 orders ('only when weylOrder(board) <= CAPS.countGamesGroup'). The stated limit, AtlasSheet.astro:266 '...not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements; this group has {sheet.weylOrder}.' and downloads.ts:124 'not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements', equals SPEC 5.6's cap. SPEC writes the same number in prose itself (5.5 'Offered for |W| <= 60000'; Appendix G 'present when |W| <= 60000'). decisions/P6-A4.md records both texts verbatim ('the count above 60000 is replaced by "The number of complete games from all ones is not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements; this group has |W|."' and the CSV row 'complete_games,,not offered for a group of more than 60000 elements'); grep finds 2 copies in DECISIONS.md. COMMON.md 4.5 'Keep caps as the specification sets them'. No value on screen or in the CSV differs from the contract or SPEC.
verdicts.reason: the cited CONTRACTS 2.3 holds no 'used once' rule. The cap decision uses CAPS.countGamesGroup, and the stated number equals SPEC 5.6's 60000 in a wording the P6-A4 plan prescribes and decisions/P6-A4.md records, so what remains is a rule found only in the lens's own attack list, not a disagreement with the specification, oracle or contract.
